autostorage.merge.merge_databases(target: autostorage.database.Database, source: autostorage.database.Database, *, commit: bool = True) → autostorage.merge.MergeReport#

Copy source’s contents into target, validating and deduplicating.

This is the lower-level function Database.merge_from wraps. Prefer target.merge_from(source) in library code; use this directly only for a functional call style (e.g. scripting) where that reads more naturally.

Rows are copied with freshly-assigned primary keys and remapped foreign keys. ModelRow, GeometryRow, non-auto-managed IdentityRows, CalculationRow, StationaryPointRow, and StageRow are deduplicated against target’s existing content; everything else is copied fresh.

InChI/conformer identities are deliberately skipped here: inserting each source StationaryPointRow fresh lets autostorage.events’s flush listeners regenerate and dedup them against target’s live state, so a conformer shared by both databases collapses onto one identity. Every copied row passes through normal ORM validation.

Only flush() is used until the end, so an error partway through leaves target unchanged.

Parameters:

  • target – Database to copy rows into.

  • source – Database to copy rows from. Only ever read, never modified.

  • commit – If True (default), commit once every table has copied successfully. If False, leave flushed-but-uncommitted for the caller.

  • optional – If True (default), commit once every table has copied successfully. If False, leave flushed-but-uncommitted for the caller.

Returns:

MergeReport – Per-table counts of rows copied and reused.

autostorage.merge._is_same_database(a: autostorage.database.Database, b: autostorage.database.Database) → bool#

Return whether a and b refer to the same underlying database.

In-memory databases (path ":memory:") never count as a match; on-disk Databases match if they resolve to the same file.

autostorage.merge._link_table_key_columns(cls: type[sqlmodel.SQLModel]) → list[str] | None#

Return cls’s primary-key column names, or None if it isn’t a link table.

A link table (BaseLink) has no own id column – its primary key is the composite of the foreign keys it joins – which is exactly the case where deduplicating either endpoint (e.g. GeometryRow/CalculationRow) can make two source rows remap onto a primary key that already exists in target.

autostorage.merge._copy_stages(*, target: autostorage.database.Database, source: autostorage.database.Database, id_map: dict[type[sqlmodel.SQLModel], dict[int, int]], copied: dict[str, int], reused: dict[str, int]) → None#

Find-or-create every source StageRow against target.

Membership is read from source’s StationaryStageLink rows rather than row.stationaries, since a plain select(StageRow) doesn’t eagerly load the relationship. StationaryStageLink itself is copied separately (its generic _copy_table pass, later in _ordered_models() order), deduped by composite primary key against the links a reused StageRow already has in target.

autostorage.merge._copy_identities(*, target: autostorage.database.Database, source: autostorage.database.Database, id_map: dict[type[sqlmodel.SQLModel], dict[int, int]], copied: dict[str, int], reused: dict[str, int]) → set[int]#

Find-or-create every non-auto-managed source IdentityRow against target.

Auto-managed identities (AUTO_MANAGED_IDENTITY_ALGORITHMS) are left for autostorage.events’s flush listeners to regenerate instead.

Returns:

set[int] – Source-side ids of skipped identities, so callers can filter out rows referencing them (identity extras, stationary-identity links).
